topic: Strategic Intellectual Property Considerations for Protecting AI Innovations in Chemical Engineering Fields
title: Strategic Intellectual Property Considerations for Protecting AI Innovations in Chemical Engineering Fields
session_title: Issues in Law for Practicing Engineers
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has significant potential for use in many fields relevant to chemical engineers. Use of AI can reduce the time and resources needed for modeling, optimization, material traceability, advance process control, and even discovery and development of novel materials. It is critical that users understand the intellectual property implications of the use of AI. This presentation will provide basic information regarding protectable components of AI-related work and tools that can be considered for protecting and monetizing resulting IP.

topic: Is the Invention a Product or a Process: Product-By-Process Claims in Practice
title: Is the Invention a Product or a Process: Product-By-Process Claims in Practice
session_title: Issues in Law for Practicing Engineers
abstract: Litigation relating to product-by-process patent claims often comes up in the chemical engineering context. A patent holder seeking to establish infringement of such a claim must prove that the accused infringer meets each of the process limitations recited in the claim; however, a party seeking to invalidate the patent only needs to establish that the product previously existed, regardless of the process by which it was made. This session will focus on what product-by-process claims are, how they are interpreted by courts, and key takeaways for those in the industry. Whether you are an expert witness, a process engineer seeking to protect or design around intellectual property, or just interested in patent law, this session is for you.

topic: Catastrophic Losses in the Chemical Industry and Subrogation – the Expert’s Perspective
title: Catastrophic Losses in the Chemical Industry and Subrogation – the Expert’s Perspective
session_title: Issues in Law for Practicing Engineers
abstract: Devasting fires and explosions can wreak havoc on a chemical processing plant. After the smoke settles and the site is safely secured, engineers begin the process of investigating the what, why, and how surrounding the incident. While many engineers may be familiar with incident investigation and associated root cause analyses, in parallel the legal and insurance industry evaluate another very important aspect of the loss – its potential for subrogation. After the loss, the facility’s insurance carrier begins the complicated process of managing the facility’s insurance claim process. While the insurance carrier provides reimbursement to the policy holder for expenses covered by the policy, the insurer has an opportunity to recover those payments if the loss is the fault of a third-party (i.e., a company that is not the insurance policy holder (first-party), or the insurance company (second-party)). If a third-party is responsible for the loss, such as negligence of a contractor performing work on site, then the insurance company can step into the shoes of their insured and initiate litigation against the liable third-party for the financial damage the insurance company has suffered. Understanding the potential for claim recovery through subrogation can become a key consideration of the investigation and legal teams in the aftermath of the incident. This presentation will review key aspects of the subrogation process, how they intersect within the broader context of incident investigation, and how engineers and attorneys can work together to efficiency navigate the process at the request of the insurance carrier.
